title: How to count workdays, rest days, and makeup workdays
description: Count workdays and rest days between two dates. Use Labor Day and Saturday makeup workday examples to verify results and handle missing holiday data.
content:
Open the workday calculator, enter the Start Date and End Date, then select Calculate Workdays. The result includes both dates and lists workdays, rest days, and total days in the range. Known makeup workdays count as workdays. If the page reports missing holiday data for a year, verify that year's official schedule before using the result.

Enter the dates and run the calculation

Enter the first day to include on the left and the last day on the right. When scheduling a project, decide whether the planned completion date is available for work. If work can continue that day, use it as the end date. If that day is reserved for delivery and work ends the day before, enter the previous day on the right.

After changing the dates, select Calculate Workdays again. Start with a schedule you know. Verify the year, month, and day in each field, then review the result. Record the inputs alongside the result in your schedule so the next person can see which dates the count covers.

  • To count the available workdays in a range, enter both endpoints.
  • To see whether a date is a workday or a rest day, enter it in both fields.
  • To find the time between dates, use the date difference calculator and verify whether the endpoints are included.

If your source only lists the start and end months, look up the actual dates in the schedule. Using the first and last days of the months counts the full months and can include days before a mid-month start. In a shared spreadsheet, put the full dates alongside the count so others can reproduce it.

Read the results

Look at the Workdays row. The total already includes the makeup workdays shown in parentheses. Adding them again would count them twice. The rest days row counts dates classified as days off under the weekend and known holiday rules. Add workdays and rest days to verify that they equal the total days in the range.

From 2026-05-01 through 2026-05-09, the page shows 4 workdays, including 1 makeup workday, and 5 rest days, for a total of 9 days. To verify the workday count, mark the range on a calendar, cross out the holiday dates, and compare the remaining workdays with the result. [S1]

You can also start with the total. Write down the number of calendar dates in the range, then put each date in a workday or rest day column. If the two counts do not add up to the calendar total, verify that you included both endpoints. Circle makeup workdays within the workday column to keep their classification clear.

Count both endpoints or look up a single day

The calculator evaluates both the start and end dates. Enter 2026-05-09 in both fields and the total is 1 day. It is a makeup workday, so the workday count is also 1. A single-day lookup shows how the date was classified and can reveal exceptions missing from a calendar or schedule. [S1]

When copying dates from another spreadsheet, review how it defines the range. For example, if the schedule says to start counting the day after work begins, enter that next day as the start date. Office's NETWORKDAYS function also includes both endpoints. Use the same dates when verifying the count and align the workday rules separately. [S4]

Use the date to verify weekend makeup workdays

For holiday adjustments, look up the date before applying the weekday rules. The calculator counts known makeup workdays as workdays and known days off as rest days. For dates without a record, it treats Saturdays and Sundays as rest days. To see why a particular Saturday counts as a workday, run a single-day calculation and compare it with the official notice.

The Labor Day schedule shows how this works. Under the schedule published by the General Office of China's State Council, 2026-05-01 through 2026-05-05 are days off, and Saturday, 2026-05-09, is a workday. Use the calendar tool to find the dates in the monthly view, then verify the exceptions against the notice. [S1]

Date rangeWorkdaysRest daysOf which makeup workdays
2026-05-01 to 2026-05-094 days5 days1 day
2026-05-01 to 2026-05-010 days1 day0 days
2026-05-09 to 2026-05-091 day0 days1 day

Record the holiday start and end dates separately from the makeup workdays. A makeup workday can fall after the holiday. If you only review dates within the holiday period, you may cross out a later makeup workday as a regular weekend day. When a holiday falls on a regular rest day, mark it once in your worksheet and subtract it once from the total. [S1]

Review the date fields when a message appears

“Please select a date range.” means a date field is empty. Fill in the missing date and run the calculation again. If the dates are reversed, the page displays “End date cannot be earlier than start date.” Verify both fields, especially when scheduling across the end of a month. Correct the date and recalculate. Look for “Calculation complete.” or a new information message to confirm the submission.

The previous result may stay visible after an error. For example, if you calculate a range, clear a date, and select the button again, the result panel still shows the previous counts. Read the status message, correct the dates, and submit again before recording the new result.

Verify missing holiday data for ranges that span years

When a range crosses into the next year, the calculator looks for holiday records for each year. For any year listed as missing data, it uses the standard weekend rules. It still uses the available records for other years and returns totals for the full range. To account for holidays and makeup workdays in a missing year, verify the dates against that year's official schedule. [S1]

Split the range by year to verify each part. End the first range on the last day of the year and start the next range on the first day of the following year. The calculator includes both endpoints of each range, so use adjacent ranges. This isolates the dates that need further verification in the range that shows the message.

A completed calculation uses the data available to the calculator. Before publishing a schedule based on the result, keep the relevant year's holiday schedule alongside it. If a notice changes or your organization uses a different schedule, verify the attendance entries directly to avoid adjusting dates you already recorded. [S1]

Limits and scheduling rules

The page gives a maximum span of 100 years. The limit applies when the difference between the dates exceeds 36600 days. If the span exceeds the limit or a date cannot be parsed, the page displays “Choose a valid range of no more than 100 years.” For a long range, recalculate it in yearly segments and verify that the segments meet without gaps.

The calculator uses a Saturday–Sunday weekend with holiday and makeup workday adjustments. If your team has different days off, rotating shifts, half days, or additional leave, record actual attendance on one row per date and total it from that schedule. The calculator accepts a single date range and outputs whole-day counts. Use the staff schedule to track hours, shifts, and organization-specific holidays. [S2]

Calculate a deadline from a workday count

If you have a start date and a planned number of workdays, you can use them to find a deadline. The calculator requires an end date, so enter a tentative deadline, see whether the range has enough workdays, and adjust the end date. Record whether the start date is available for work so you can reproduce the count later.

To calculate the date directly in a spreadsheet, use WORKDAY in Google Sheets to find the end date after a given number of workdays. WORKDAY.INTL in Excel also lets you set the weekly days off. Before passing in a holiday list, verify that it contains the dates you want to exclude and record local makeup workdays separately. This determines whether the spreadsheet date matches the adjusted holiday calendar. [S5] [S6]

Resolve differences with Excel or Google Sheets

Excel's NETWORKDAYS.INTL lets you specify weekly days off and exclude dates using the holiday argument. If you configure a Saturday–Sunday weekend and enter the Labor Day holidays, Saturday still counts as a weekend day. To verify a count that includes makeup workdays, flag each day's attendance in a separate column. Count makeup workdays first, then exclude holidays and regular weekend days. Excel returns a negative value for reversed dates. The calculator displays a date error. [S1] [S2]

Google Sheets' NETWORKDAYS counts workdays in a date range. In the formula, reference cells that contain dates. A slash-separated date entered directly as an argument may be interpreted as division. When comparing the results, verify that the formula recognized the arguments as dates, then align the weekend rules and holiday list. [S3]

If the counts differ by one day, find the date the two methods classify differently. Narrow the range to the first half and see if the difference persists, then narrow it to a single day. If both methods classify the date the same way, verify whether either method excludes the start or delivery date and whether you submitted the new dates when recalculating.

Record the inputs and results for handoff

Record the start and end dates and state that the count includes both. Copy the workday, makeup workday, and rest day counts into their respective columns. If you subtract rest days from calendar days, use the same date range so the spreadsheets cover the same dates.

For holiday periods, recalculate a disputed date on its own and record whether it counts as a workday or a rest day. For ranges that span years, record the years the page lists as missing holiday data and fill in the exceptions you can verify from official notices. Share the workday count once the staff schedule and date range are aligned. [S1]

faqs.q: Does the workday count include the start and end dates?
faqs.a: Yes. Both dates are evaluated using holiday records and the day of the week. Enter the same date in both fields to count only that day.

faqs.q: Do I need to add makeup workdays separately?
faqs.a: The workday total already includes the makeup workdays shown in parentheses.

faqs.q: How are workdays counted when holiday data is missing?
faqs.a: The calculator applies standard weekend rules to years with missing data and uses available holiday records for the other years.
